name: Materials Project
description: Open database of DFT-computed properties (formation energies, band structures, elastic tensors, phase diagrams, X-ray spectra) for over 150,000 inorganic crystalline materials, plus molecules and battery electrodes. Data are generated by high-throughput VASP DFT workflows.
associated_paper: Jain et al., 'Commentary: The Materials Project', APL Materials 1, 011002 (2013)

name: Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD)
description: Database of DFT-calculated thermodynamic and structural properties for over 1 million inorganic compounds, focused on formation energies, phase stability and convex hulls. Generated by high-throughput DFT calculations at Northwestern University.
associated_paper: Kirklin et al., 'The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD)', npj Comput. Mater. 1, 15010 (2015)

name: AFLOW (Automatic FLOW for Materials Discovery)
description: One of the largest computational materials repositories, with DFT-calculated properties for over 3.5 million compounds and hundreds of millions of properties, including thermodynamic, electronic, mechanical and thermal descriptors. Generated by automated high-throughput ab-initio workflows.
associated_paper: Curtarolo et al., 'AFLOW: An automatic framework for high-throughput materials discovery', Comput. Mater. Sci. 58 (2012)

name: NOMAD (Novel Materials Discovery) Repository & Archive
description: Large FAIR repository and archive of raw and processed computational materials-science data (millions of DFT and beyond-DFT calculations from many codes), with growing support for experimental data uploads. Community-contributed and code-agnostic.
associated_paper: Draxl & Scheffler, 'The NOMAD laboratory: from data sharing to artificial intelligence', J. Phys. Mater. 2, 036001 (2019)

name: JARVIS-NIST (Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations)
description: NIST infrastructure and databases (JARVIS-DFT, JARVIS-FF, JARVIS-ML, JARVIS-Leaderboard) covering ~80,000 materials with ~1 million calculated properties spanning DFT, force fields, and ML models, plus some experimental references. Generated by automated simulation workflows.
associated_paper: Choudhary et al., 'The joint automated repository for various integrated simulations (JARVIS)', npj Comput. Mater. 6, 173 (2020)

name: Materials Cloud Archive
description: FAIR, open-access archive hosting hundreds of community-contributed materials-science datasets (often with full provenance via AiiDA), spanning DFT calculations, workflows and some experimental data. Each dataset receives a persistent DOI.
associated_paper: Talirz et al., 'Materials Cloud, a platform for open computational science', Sci. Data 7, 299 (2020)

name: Citrination / Open Citrination (Citrine Informatics)
description: Large open materials and chemicals data platform aggregating experimental property data contributed by users and auto-extracted from the literature, alongside computational data. The public platform has been decommissioned but datasets remain accessible via their DOIs/URLs.
associated_paper: O'Mara et al., 'Materials Data Infrastructure: A Case Study of the Citrination Platform', JOM 68 (2016)

name: Crystallography Open Database (COD)
description: Open-access collection of over 520,000 experimentally determined crystal structures of organic, inorganic, metal-organic compounds and minerals (excluding biopolymers), stored as CIF files. Structures are curated from the published literature and community contributions. Used by both the materials and chemistry communities.
associated_paper: Gražulis et al., 'Crystallography Open Database (COD)', Nucleic Acids Res. 40, D420 (2012)

name: American Mineralogist Crystal Structure Database (AMCSD)
description: Freely accessible database of experimentally determined crystal structures of minerals and related materials, drawn from American Mineralogist, The Canadian Mineralogist, European Journal of Mineralogy and other sources. Searchable by mineral, chemistry, cell parameters and symmetry; served via the RRUFF Project.
associated_paper: Downs & Hall-Wallace, 'The American Mineralogist Crystal Structure Database', American Mineralogist 88 (2003)

name: Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20)
description: Large benchmark dataset for ML interatomic potentials in heterogeneous catalysis, comprising ~1.28 million DFT relaxations (~265 million single-point calculations) of adsorbate-catalyst systems across diverse surfaces with N, C and O chemistries. Generated by DFT.
associated_paper: Chanussot et al., 'The Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) Dataset and Community Challenges', ACS Catal. 11 (2021)

name: Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22)
description: Extension of the Open Catalyst effort to oxide electrocatalysts, comprising 62,331 DFT relaxations (~9.85 million single-point calculations) across a range of oxide materials, coverages and adsorbates. Generated by DFT.
associated_paper: Tran et al., 'The Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) Dataset and Challenges for Oxide Electrocatalysts', ACS Catal. 13 (2023)

name: Catalysis-Hub.org
description: Open electronic-structure database for surface reactions containing more than 100,000 chemisorption and reaction energies from DFT calculations, with surface geometries and calculation parameters, plus tools and a Python/GraphQL API. Generated by DFT (largely SUNCAT/Stanford).
associated_paper: Winther et al., 'Catalysis-Hub.org, an open electronic structure database for surface reactions', Sci. Data 6, 75 (2019)

name: BatteryArchive.org
description: Public repository for visualization, analysis and comparison of experimental battery cycling data across institutions, aggregating datasets (e.g. from Sandia, NREL, CALCE, Oxford) converted to a common format with cycle- and time-series data. Data are experimental cell-testing measurements.
associated_paper: Dos Reis et al., 'Lithium-ion battery data and where to find it', Energy and AI (2021)

name: TRI/MIT/Stanford Fast-Charging Battery Dataset (Severson & Attia)
description: Widely used experimental dataset of 124 commercial LFP/graphite cells (plus a follow-on 45-cell set) cycled under 72 fast-charging protocols, with cycle lives from ~150 to 2,300 cycles. Provided in CSV/MATLAB/JSON formats by the Toyota Research Institute D3BATT collaboration.
associated_paper: Severson et al., 'Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation', Nat. Energy 4 (2019)

name: The Perovskite Database Project
description: Open-access, FAIR database of experimental perovskite solar cell devices, covering more than 42,000 cells with up to ~100 parameters each (device stack, composition, J-V metrics, stability), curated from over 16,000 publications. Every entry is linked to its source DOI; searchable and downloadable, now also hosted in NOMAD.
associated_paper: Jacobsson et al., 'An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles', Nat. Energy 7 (2022)

name: SuperCon (NIMS / MDR)
description: Curated database of experimental superconducting materials recording chemical composition and critical temperature (Tc) for tens of thousands of conventional and unconventional superconductors. Re-edited and released as MDR SuperCon (~26,000 records) via the NIMS Materials Data Repository.
associated_paper: NIMS MDR SuperCon Datasheet (re-edited from the NIMS SuperCon / MatNavi database)

name: ESTM — Experimentally Synthesized Thermoelectric Materials Dataset
description: Public dataset of 5,205 experimental observations covering 880 unique experimentally synthesized thermoelectric materials, with measured Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, power factor and figure of merit (ZT). Released with the SIMD data-driven discovery toolkit.
associated_paper: Na & Chang, 'A public database of thermoelectric materials and system-identified material representation for data-driven discovery', npj Comput. Mater. 8 (2022)

name: Computational 2D Materials Database (C2DB)
description: Open database of structural, thermodynamic, elastic, electronic, magnetic and optical properties for ~4,000+ two-dimensional monolayers across more than 40 crystal structures. Properties are computed with DFT and, for select materials, many-body methods (G0W0/BSE) using GPAW.
associated_paper: Haastrup et al., 'The Computational 2D Materials Database (C2DB)', 2D Mater. 5, 042002 (2018)

name: 2DMatPedia
description: Open computational database of more than 6,000 two-dimensional monolayer structures obtained via top-down exfoliation screening of the Materials Project and bottom-up elemental substitution, with consistently calculated structural, electronic and energetic properties. Generated by DFT.
associated_paper: Zhou et al., '2DMatPedia, an open computational database of two-dimensional materials', Sci. Data 6, 86 (2019)

name: Matbench
description: Curated benchmark suite of 13 supervised ML tasks (312 to ~132,000 samples) for materials property prediction, drawing on 10 DFT-derived and experimental data sources, with an automated public leaderboard. Maintained by the Materials Project.
associated_paper: Dunn et al., 'Benchmarking materials property prediction methods: the Matbench test set and Automatminer reference algorithm', npj Comput. Mater. 6 (2020)

name: Matbench Discovery
description: Benchmark framework and leaderboard for evaluating ML energy models (interatomic potentials, one-shot predictors) on their ability to discover stable inorganic crystals via WBM/thermodynamic-stability tasks. Built on DFT reference data from the Materials Project ecosystem.
associated_paper: Riebesell et al., 'Matbench Discovery', Nature Machine Intelligence (2025)

name: matminer Datasets
description: Collection of standardized, benchmark-ready materials datasets bundled with the matminer data-mining toolkit and hosted on Figshare, spanning experimental and DFT-derived properties loadable directly as pandas dataframes. Aggregated from published sources for ML benchmarking.
associated_paper: Ward et al., 'Matminer: An open source toolkit for materials data mining', Comput. Mater. Sci. 152 (2018)

name: High-Throughput Experimental Materials Database (HTEM-DB, NREL)
description: First large publicly available collection of experimental data for inorganic thin-film materials synthesized by combinatorial high-throughput methods at NREL, covering synthesis conditions, chemical composition, crystal structure and optoelectronic property measurements for tens of thousands of samples. Data are experimental, accessible via web UI and API.
associated_paper: Zakutayev et al., 'An open experimental database for exploring inorganic materials', Sci. Data 5, 180053 (2018)

name: Starrydata2
description: Open, web-based database that crowdsources experimental material-property data digitized from published plot images, containing 190,000+ curves from 80,000+ physical samples across 13,000+ papers, heavily weighted toward experimental thermoelectric materials. All data are openly downloadable.
associated_paper: Katsura et al., 'Data-driven analysis of electron relaxation times ... / Starrydata', Sci. Technol. Adv. Mater. (2019)
